name: Umbra Desolation
specific_features: Shadow zones that absorb all electromagnetic radiation anomalously
description: Umbra Desolation is a lifeless world of grey regolith and stark shadows, its airless surface exposed to the full brutality of its star's radiation on the dayside while the nightside languishes in deep cold. Permanently shadowed polar craters have accumulated deposits of volatile ices over billions of years, their floors never touched by direct sunlight. Collapsed lava tube systems from an ancient volcanic era scar the surface with irregular trenches and sinkholes.

Without atmosphere, the surface exists in absolute silence and merciless clarity. Every crater rim, every rock, every grain of regolith casts a shadow with razor-sharp edges, the transition from blazing light to utter darkness occurring within the width of a particle. The thermal shock of crossing from sun to shadow is immediate and severe, stressing materials and equipment that must endure both extremes.

The permanently shadowed craters exhibit an anomalous property: they absorb electromagnetic radiation at all measured wavelengths far more efficiently than their composition would suggest. Radar, lidar, and radio signals directed into these craters do not return, as if the shadows themselves consume the energy. Analysis of the crater floor materials shows nothing unusual, yet the absorption effect persists. The phenomenon has defied explanation through three major research campaigns.

Umbra Desolation's mineral resources are modest but accessible, making it a viable mining prospect for regional operations. The collapsed lava tubes offer potential shelter for subsurface installations. The anomalous shadow craters remain off-limits pending further study, their perimeters marked with automated warning beacons that occasionally malfunction when positioned too close to the shadow boundary.
